title: DWG/DXF DIMJOGANG angle-unit conversion
scope: Normalize the AC1021+ DWG DIMJOGANG radians value to the degree-valued DXF/API representation
Apply the inverse conversion when writing DIMSTYLE and HEADER DWG values
Keep the existing DXF group-code and system-variable values in degrees

formatReferences.title: Autodesk DXF group codes in numerical order
formatReferences.finding: Group codes 50 through 58 are angles output in degrees to DXF files and radians through AutoLISP and ObjectARX applications.

formatReferences.title: Autodesk DIMJOGANG system variable
formatReferences.finding: The setting's documented valid range is 5 through 90 degrees.

formatReferences.title: Open Design Specification for .dwg files v5.4.1, §20.4.68
formatReferences.finding: R2007+ DIMSTYLE stores DIMJOGANG as a BD body field. The spec does not state the unit; the radians interpretation is corroborated by the producer sample below.

producerSource.finding: The typed import probe observed DIMJOGANG 0.785398 in the MEP DIMSTYLE (approximately pi/4). With conversion enabled, dwg2dxf succeeds and emits 45 for both the DXF $DIMJOGANG header variable and the MEP DIMSTYLE group 50. This is one Autodesk-authored sample profile, not a general producer/version qualification.

localSource.finding: DIMSTYLE parsing converts radians to degrees before typed synchronization; its DWG encoder converts degrees back to radians. HEADER DWG parsing and encoding apply the corresponding conversion, while DXF parsing/writing retain the public degree value.

generatedCodecControl.result: PASS; independent wire walk confirms a 45-degree API value encodes as pi/4 radians and production DWG parser returns 45 degrees

producerConversion.fixturePolicy: Source DWG and generated DXF remain outside the repository.

limits: Only DIMJOGANG's R2007+ DWG/API radians and DXF degrees boundary is addressed.
The DWG spec identifies the field type and location but does not explicitly document its unit; one producer source plus DXF/API conventions supports the conversion.
The generated vector is parser/encoder consistency evidence; the local AC1024 producer conversion independently confirms the read-to-DXF path, not native application write/read interoperability.
